title: Priority-based request admission controller and customer bridge for 5xx escalations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several high-severity customer escalations during recent tenant surges revealed correlated 5xx waves driven by uncontrolled retry amplification and long-lived streaming requests. This ticket implements a priority-aware admission controller at the edge proxy plus a short-circuit customer-bridge so that paying/high-priority tenants can maintain service during global degradation. The goal is to reduce system-wide 5xx blast radius, provide deterministic fast-fail semantics for lower-priority traffic, and offer a controlled emergency fastpath for escalated customers without bypassing quota/accounting.
mitigation_steps: Add per-tenant priority weight and sliding admission window to edge proxy
Introduce signed idempotency token policy to allow fast-rejects for duplicate retries
Implement customer-bridge route that maps tenant IDs to emergency admission tokens
Throttle long-lived streaming request admission during surge windows
Expose new metrics: tenant_admit_rate, tenant_dropped_retries, bridge_fastpath_usage
rollback_plan: Revert proxy config toggle and disable customer-bridge feature flag. The admission controller is behind a runtime feature flag and supports immediate disable via config push. If rollback is required, we will switch to legacy admission behavior and scale up standby pool nodes while alerting SREs.
acceptance_criteria: Edge proxy enforces per-tenant priority admission and logs decision traces
Overall 5xx rate reduces by >= 40% during controlled load tests resembling customer surge
Critical tenants using customer-bridge observe <2x latency increase and <1% error rate during surge scenario
All new metrics ingested into console dashboards with 1m granularity and alerts configured
test_plan: Synthetic tenant-surge test in staging: 300k concurrent inflight requests simulated with mixed priorities
Chaos test: flip feature flag mid-surge and verify graceful failover
Idempotency token fuzzing to verify signed tokens are validated and duplicates fast-failed
Run integration with Dedicated cluster simulator to ensure admission config is respected in reservation-aware proxy
updates: 2026-03-11: Spike completed to validate admission algorithm; observed token signing latency ~2ms on edge nodes
2026-03-12: Design review with SRE and Product; agreed on metrics and alert thresholds; customer-bridge policy must be auditable
2026-03-13: Initial implementation pushed: edge proxy accepts priority header and token signature check (PR linked)
2026-03-15: Staging surge test ran; preliminary numbers show 42% reduction in systemic 5xxs but noticed increased retry failures for low-priority tenants; tuning in progress
notes: Dedicated and Private installs will ship admission controller as opt-in config and provide a CLI toggle for on-prem ops
Billing/usage must still record bridge fastpath consumption to prevent unmetered bypass
We must coordinate a customer comms template for customers gated into the bridge explaining expected behavior and temporary limits
postmortem_actions: Add synthetic tenant-surge alarms to detect early retry amplification patterns
Create an engineering doc describing safe idempotency token lifetime and revocation model
Schedule tabletop with Solutions Eng to practice customer bridge activation
observability_tasks: Create per-tenant rate panels in Console
Anchor alerts: tenant_admit_rate_drop > 60% for 5m and spike in tenant_dropped_retries
Add tracing span to capture admission decision path for every request
